Command: Do Not Blaspheme the Name of the LORD
Summary: Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death — the whole congregation stones him. The command itself is distinct from the live Do Not Misuse God's Name row (Exodus 20:7, vain use); this is direct cursing and reviling of God's name, given after the blasphemer's case in Leviticus 24.
Commandment: Do not blaspheme — curse or revile — the name of the LORD.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as moral. The penalty belonged to Israel's theocratic court and is not carried into Christian church discipline, which answers blasphemy with witness and, where needed, exclusion from fellowship — but the prohibition itself is repeated: blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is the one sin Jesus says will not be forgiven (Matthew 12:31-32), and reverence for God's name remains the first petition of the Lord's Prayer.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: the name is God's own self-disclosure, so cursing it strikes at God himself, not merely at a word. Scripture states the prohibition and penalty without a separate reason (Leviticus 24:16).
